title: EPFO urges establishments to utilize the Employees’ Enrolment Campaign, 2026 to ensure social security for employees outside EPF coverage
body_text:
The Employees’ Provident Fund Organisation (EPFO) has urged establishments to utilize the Employees’ Enrolment Campaign, 2026 (EEC 2026) notified with effect from 29 June 2026, which provides a special one-time opportunity to enrol eligible employees who remained outside EPF coverage during the period 1 April 2009 to 31 March 2026.
The Campaign will remain open up to 31 October 2026 and is aimed at facilitating voluntary compliance by employers and extending the benefits of provident fund, pension and insurance to eligible workers.
Under EEC 2026, eligible employers can declare and enrol employees who were left out of EPF coverage during the prescribed period and are alive and continuing in employment with the establishment on the date of declaration. The Campaign provides specified relaxations to facilitate regularisation of past compliance, including waiver of the employee’s share where it was not deducted earlier, subject to the conditions of the Campaign.
Employers are required to complete the enrolment and remittance process through the prescribed online mechanism. A Face Authentication-based UAN is to be generated through the UMANG App for each declared employee, and contributions are to be remitted through the Electronic Challan-cum-Return (ECR).
The Campaign is intended to benefit establishments and workers by providing a structured mechanism for bringing eligible employees within the statutory social security framework. Employers are encouraged to review their employment and wage records and identify eligible employees who may have remained outside EPF coverage during the prescribed period.
EPFO is also undertaking extensive awareness and outreach activities to disseminate the salient features of EEC 2026 among employers, employees, establishments, contractors and other stakeholders. Ministries and Departments of the Government of India, State Governments and Union Territories, Public Sector Undertakings, Autonomous Bodies and other organisations are being encouraged to facilitate wider dissemination of the Campaign among establishments and service providers under their administrative control.
Employers are encouraged to make use of this one-time opportunity and complete the enrolment of eligible employees before the Campaign closes on 31 October 2026.
***
Rini Choudhury

enrichment.summary: EPFO has launched the Employees' Enrolment Campaign 2026 (EEC 2026), effective from 29 June 2026 and open till 31 October 2026, giving employers a one-time opportunity to enrol employees who were left out of EPF coverage between 1 April 2009 and 31 March 2026. The campaign offers relaxations such as waiver of the employee's share of contribution where it was not previously deducted, and requires enrolment via a Face Authentication-based UAN generated through UMANG, with contributions remitted through the Electronic Challan-cum-Return (ECR). EPFO is conducting outreach to employers, PSUs, and government bodies to maximise voluntary compliance and extend provident fund, pension, and insurance benefits to previously uncovered workers.
enrichment.context:
EPFO periodically runs enrolment campaigns to bring workers who were technically eligible but never formally registered under EPF coverage into the social security net, since many employers historically failed to report or deduct contributions for eligible staff. Such campaigns balance the goal of extending social security (Article 41-linked Directive Principles, and India's broader push towards universalising social security envisaged under the Code on Social Security, 2020) against practical realities of enforcement, by offering employers amnesty-like relaxations (e.g., waiver of unpaid employee shares) to encourage voluntary disclosure rather than punitive recovery.

This fits into EPFO's ongoing digitisation and Aadhaar/UMANG-based service delivery reforms aimed at reducing compliance friction — a continuation of measures like UAN-Aadhaar seeding and online ECR filing that have been central to widening formal social security coverage in India's largely informal labour market. Such campaigns are also relevant to discussions on formalisation of employment and the low social security coverage ratio among India's workforce, a recurring concern for policymakers and international bodies like the ILO.

prelims_questions.question: The Employees' Enrolment Campaign (EEC) 2026 launched by EPFO allows employers to enrol employees who remained outside EPF coverage during which period?
prelims_questions.explanation: As per the release, EEC 2026 covers employees left out of EPF coverage between 1 April 2009 and 31 March 2026.

prelims_questions.question: Under EEC 2026, the Universal Account Number (UAN) for declared employees is to be generated using which mechanism?
prelims_questions.explanation: The release states that a Face Authentication-based UAN is to be generated through the UMANG App for each declared employee.

mains_questions.question: Discuss the role of periodic enrolment campaigns like the EPFO's Employees' Enrolment Campaign in extending social security coverage to India's workforce. What structural challenges hinder universal social security coverage in India?

Examine how digital initiatives such as UAN generation through UMANG and Electronic Challan-cum-Return (ECR) have transformed compliance and service delivery in India's social security administration.

study_notes.reason: The release is essentially a scheme notification with specific, testable parameters (dates, mechanism, relaxations); it offers little analytical depth beyond the standard formalisation/social-security-coverage narrative already well covered by other EPFO measures.

prelims.point: Employees' Enrolment Campaign 2026 (EEC 2026) is effective from 29 June 2026 to 31 October 2026, covering employees left out of EPF coverage between 1 April 2009 and 31 March 2026
prelims.why_important: Specific scheme name with defined effective dates and coverage period is a classic UPSC prelims statement-based question format.

prelims.point: EEC 2026 waives the employee's share of contribution where it was not deducted earlier, as a relaxation to encourage voluntary employer compliance
prelims.why_important: Tests understanding of the specific relaxation mechanism distinguishing this campaign from routine EPF enrolment.

prelims.point: Enrolment under EEC 2026 requires a Face Authentication-based UAN generated through the UMANG App, with contributions remitted via Electronic Challan-cum-Return (ECR)
prelims.why_important: Tests knowledge of EPFO's digital compliance tools (UAN, UMANG, ECR) which are recurring technical terms in EPFO-related questions.

prelims.point: EPFO (Employees' Provident Fund Organisation) functions under the Ministry of Labour & Employment and administers provident fund, pension and insurance benefits
prelims.why_important: Basic institutional fact about EPFO's parent ministry and mandate is foundational for any EPFO-related prelims question.

mains.point: Amnesty-style enrolment campaigns reflect a policy choice to prioritise voluntary compliance over punitive enforcement to widen social security coverage
mains.analytical_use: Useful for questions on strategies to extend social security to India's informal/under-covered workforce and the trade-offs between enforcement and incentive-based compliance.

mains.point: Such campaigns highlight the persistent gap between statutory EPF eligibility and actual employer compliance in India's labour market
mains.analytical_use: Can be deployed in answers on challenges in achieving universal social security coverage and the Code on Social Security, 2020.

low_priority.point: EPFO's outreach and awareness activities involving ministries, PSUs, and state governments

low_priority.point: General encouragement to employers to review records and enrol employees before closure
